design.summary: Five-finger tendon hand: 5 MG996R flexion servos in the forearm, an MG90S thumb swing, 16 joints, squeezes about 10 N, holds about 1.17 kg

uses: Arduino Nano (serial commands from the PC)
5 V 10 A servo supply (V+ terminal of the PCA9685)

performance.actuator: TowerPro MG996R standard servo (metal gears) + round horn
performance.mount: rear flange, 4 x M6 on PCD 50 (fits the arms' tool flange)
performance.cost_breakdown: parts 56.00 USD, filament 14.48 USD (0.58 kg), fasteners ~8.25 USD, wiring 10.34 USD

assumptions: Each finger is underactuated: one tendon over three joints, elastic cord on the back to open it. The middle and end joints are modelled as following the base joint (mimic); a real tendon finger also wraps round an object's shape.
Fingertip forces use the MG996R's rated torque (not its stall torque) through a 6 mm spool: a household-object hand (cups, fruit, small tools), not a crushing grip.
Glue silicone pads (or print TPU caps) on the fingertips and palm: the grip numbers assume friction 0.6.

notes: Mains side: IEC inlet to the supply's AC terminals with insulated spades, earth wired first, case closed before plugging in. Have it checked if you are not qualified to wire mains.
The Nano runs from its USB cable (serial commands from the PC); the servos from the adapter. Servo leads are extended to the forearm in one braided sleeve.
